notes:
An audit given a five-minute limit could spend twenty checking outbound links.

Docket's `--max-seconds` is described, on the command line and in the code beside it, as a wall-clock limit — a hard ceiling on how long an audit runs. The crawl honoured it. The phase that runs afterwards, checking whether your outbound links still work, had no deadline of any kind.

That was harmless while a link check cost milliseconds. It stops being harmless when a site asks to be crawled slowly.

Docket obeys `Crawl-delay` in robots.txt, and it obeys it properly: the delay is a genuine gap between requests for the whole crawler, not a gap per worker, because four workers each pausing ten seconds still make four requests every ten seconds. That is the right way to be polite and it is not changing.

The arithmetic is what nobody had done. Docket checks up to sixty outbound links and twenty share images. On a federal government portal that asks for ten seconds between requests, eighty requests at ten seconds each is **eight hundred seconds** — thirteen minutes and twenty seconds of link checking, after the crawl, on an audit that had been given five minutes in total. We ran exactly that audit and killed it at thirteen minutes twenty-two.

The sixty-link cap exists for this reason already. Its own note says sampling was added because "a site with 3,000 outbound links would take longer to link-check than to crawl". At ten seconds a request, sixty links does that too — the cap was counting the wrong thing.

So the sample is now limited by the time remaining as well as by the count. When the budget is generous, nothing changes and every selected link is checked. When it is not, Docket checks what it can afford and the finding says how many it looked at, which it already did: "Checked 44 of the site's outbound links (a sample — not every outbound link on the site)".

**Sites that declare no crawl delay — the overwhelming majority — are entirely unaffected.** There is no time cap to hit when requests cost milliseconds, and the change is written so that a crawl with time to spare still checks every target it selected.
